As such, I can say that because there weren't also any amendments or any other reasons to, I do not intend to exercise the veto rights that come with the legislation and the 2026 budget is considered adopted as of the date.
When we're done, as we have done the last two years, we will pass a motion that Council authorizes staff to implement the budget as it has been presented.
I do want to just highlight a few of the things that were a focus of the budget.
And I think it's important to note that this being the fourth budget of this four-year term of council,
the budget actually has ensured that during these four years,
we have brought in an average property tax increase that's below the average increase of CPI in the province of Ontario.
The budget builds on the success of our previous budget and continues to address priorities that are important to our city.
From affordable city services that deliver programs and services that residents and businesses rely on,
to smart investments in infrastructure that help to address the city's asset replacement and growth-related needs,
to focusing on the future and providing funding to implement the city's 2023-26 strategic plan that is helping shape Kitchener's future.

The proposed tax increase of 2.2% maintains our existing service levels for the approximately 50 core services that the city provides and still allows our city to respond to growth-related pressures that come with welcoming new residents to Kitchener each year.
As was noted by our CFO during the budget presentation, Kitchener has one of the lowest tax levies per capita in the province when compared to other large municipalities in Ontario.
And we also have a low municipal burden, which accounts for property taxes and utility rates, making this one of the most affordable cities in the entire province.
When we consider the budget, there are a number of things to highlight in terms of investments that are included in the budget.

Of course, the most significant being the completion of the Cowan Recreation Center and its opening later this year, as well as the full opening of the Williamsburg Community Center, the Southwest Community Library, and so on, all of which have been budgeted for from a capital perspective.
We continue to make investments in housing using both our federal housing accelerator funding as well as funding from the province of Ontario and its Building Faster Fund.
There's $2.4 million for trail upgrades in the budget, $1 million for energy-efficient investments in facilities supporting our goals of corporate climate action,
